scenario: AiTA for not trusting a delivery driver? | Today I ordered food off of an app- it's a third party delivery service that picks up the food and delivers your order. Once you pay online, you're given a code that you give to the delivery driver once he gives you your food (I assume that's how the drivers get paid). The app generates a time that you can expect to get your food by, and the drivers are expected to complete the delivery by then, so if you don't get your order by the promised time you often get a percentage of your order cost refunded. Drivers are not limited in how many orders they can pick up simultaneously (they use their discretion to pick up the tickets they want), but if they take too many at once, they will exceed the time limit and most likely suffer a penalty. ​ I had ordered one tea and 2 pastries, for which I only received one. I called the shop and the manager was very apologetic, offering to using the service to send me out the missing pastry ASAP. I had assumed they would just refund me through the app, but that solution was fine too. The shop paid the delivery fee, and I was given the code to give to the driver when my order arrived. About twenty minutes later, the driver called me to ask for the code, stating he was on his way. I thanked him for letting me know he was coming and hung up, to which he called back two minutes later asking for the code again. I replied that I would have it for him the minute he arrived. After another two minutes, he called back again telling me he was nearby and he was running out of time, could he have the code? I told him he would get the code when I got my food. This time I was a bit annoyed, as he knows the rules as a driver and the only way I can guarantee that my food will be delivered is to hold onto the code until my food is here. The guy snapped at me: do you not understand the code is about to expire?! And I retorted back: Well, you better hurry then, right? as nicely as possible before hanging up. I didn't want to argue any longer, but I wasn't about to risk not getting my item by giving up the code. My friend told me that I was being selfish and unkind since the guy might not get paid for the delivery. I argued that since he voluntarily picked up the ticket, he shouldn't have taken ones he couldn't deliver on time. He said something to the effect of, "thank goodness the world isn't full of unkind bitches like you". ​ So, AItA? Should I have just given him the code and trusted he would still bring me my food? ​ The end of the story is, after I refused to tell him the code, I never heard from him again nor did I see my pastry. The shop manager saw the order wasn't marked as delivered and called to ask what happened, to which I told her the details. She tried to call the delivery guy then, but he had turned off his phone, so she apologized profusely, refunded me through the app, and reported him to the delivery service management. The manager said that he will either be severely disciplined or fired over this.

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether I should have just given the delivery driver the code and trusted him to bring my food, or if I was right to hold onto it until I got my missing pastry. Let me break this down step by step. First, I ordered some food through an app, and it's a third-party delivery service. That means the driver picks up the food from the shop and delivers it to me. Once I pay online, I get a code that I give to the driver when I receive my food. I assume that's how they get paid. The app also gives an estimated time for delivery, and if the driver doesn't deliver on time, they might get a penalty or not get paid fully. Drivers can pick up as many orders as they want, but if they take too many, they might not make it on time, which could lead to penalties. In my case, I ordered one tea and two pastries, but I only received one. I called the shop, and the manager was really sorry and offered to send the missing pastry ASAP. I thought they might just refund me through the app, but this solution was fine too. The shop paid the delivery fee, and I was given the code to give to the driver when my order arrived. About twenty minutes later, the driver called me to ask for the code, saying he was on his way. I thanked him for letting me know and hung up. Two minutes later, he called back again, asking for the code. I told him I would have it ready when he arrived. Another two minutes later, he called again, saying he was nearby and running out of time, and asked if he could have the code. I said he would get the code when I got my food. At this point, I was a bit annoyed because he knows the rules as a driver, and the only way I can guarantee my food is delivered is by holding onto the code until I get it. He snapped at me, saying, "Do you not understand the code is about to expire?!" I retorted, "Well, you better hurry then, right?" as nicely as possible before hanging up. I didn't want to argue anymore, but I wasn't about to risk not getting my item by giving up the code. My friend told me I was being selfish and unkind because the guy might not get paid for the delivery. I argued that since he voluntarily picked up the ticket, he should have taken only what he could deliver on time. My friend said something like, "Thank goodness the world isn't full of unkind bitches like you." So, the question is: Should I have just given him the code and trusted he would still bring me my food? The end of the story is that after I refused to tell him the code, I never heard from him again, and I didn't get my pastry. The shop manager saw the order wasn't marked as delivered and called to ask what happened. I told her the details, and she tried to call the delivery guy, but he had turned off his phone. So, she apologized profusely, refunded me through the app, and reported him to the delivery service management. The manager said he will either be severely disciplined or fired over this. Okay, so now I need to think about whether I was right or wrong in not giving the driver the code. Let's consider the different aspects: 1. **Understanding the System**: The delivery system relies on codes to confirm delivery and payment. If the code is given before the delivery is complete, the driver might not have an incentive to ensure the delivery is done properly. 2. **Trust Issues**: I didn't trust the driver to deliver the missing pastry after he had already failed to deliver it initially. Trust is a big factor here. 3. **Rules and Penalties**: The driver knows the rules, and if he exceeds the time limit, he might face penalties or not get paid. By holding onto the code, I was ensuring that the delivery was completed as per the agreement. 4. **Empathy and Kindness**: My friend accused me of being unkind. Is it kind to trust someone who might not follow through, especially if it affects their livelihood? 5. **Consequences of My Action**: By not giving the code, I ensured that I wouldn't be without my order, but it also led to the driver not getting paid and potentially facing discipline or losing his job. 6. **Alternative Solutions**: Could there have been a better way to handle this situation without withholding the code? Maybe communicating more clearly or finding a middle ground. 7. **Responsibility**: As a customer, do I have a responsibility to help ensure that drivers are paid fairly, or is it solely the driver's responsibility to manage their deliveries? 8. **Fairness**: Is it fair for me to hold onto the code if the driver is already in a tight spot with time? Or is it fair for the driver to expect me to trust him without any guarantee? 9. **Potential for Misuse**: If I gave the code and the driver didn't deliver, would that set a bad precedent for future deliveries? 10. **Outcome**: In the end, I didn't get my pastry, and the driver faced consequences. Was that a better outcome than risking not getting my food? Considering all these points, I need to weigh the importance of each aspect. On one hand, holding onto the code ensured that I received my order, which is my primary concern as a customer. On the other hand, withholding the code affected the driver's ability to get paid and could have negative consequences for him. I also need to think about the broader implications. If every customer withholds codes when they're not satisfied, it could create a problematic system where drivers are penalized unfairly, and customers don't get their orders. Alternatively, if customers always give codes upfront, it might lead to more instances of incomplete deliveries. In this specific situation, the driver had already failed to deliver the complete order once. Trust was broken, and there was no guarantee that giving the code again would result in the missing pastry being delivered. Therefore, holding onto the code was a way to ensure that the delivery was completed as agreed. However, it's also important to consider the driver's perspective. He was likely under time pressure and might have been trying to complete as many deliveries as possible to earn more. Withholding the code could have added unnecessary stress and potentially led to him losing his job. In conclusion, while my action of not giving the code was a way to protect myself from not receiving my order, it also had negative consequences for the driver. It's a tough situation where both parties have valid concerns.
